item.title: He went on to become an English teacher and he brings the kids he teaches, who don't have a lot of money, to this bookshop every month and buys them a book.
item.description: ​Started giving him books. “Damaged copies. Can’t sell them. You want?” He knew better. Took them anyway. Read everything. Three years of this. He aged out of foster care. Eighteen. Scared. Nowhere to go. Helped him apply to college. Scholarships. Got in. Full ride. English major. Graduated. He’s a teacher now. High school English. Brings his whole class to the bookstore. Shows them where he spent his teenage years. “Bookstore worker gave me sanctuary. Knowledge. Hope. Taught me one person caring changes trajectories.” He buys books for students. Who can’t afford them. Pays it forward. Every kid in his class reads. Because someone let a foster kid read for free.

item.title: GovBrief Today #618
item.description: Donald Trump’s Justice Department announced an antitrust investigation today into the TV pool networks that refused to cover for CNN. Last month Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News answered by suspending the pool coverage they share, and a federal judge restored the three outlets’ access, finding they were likely denied due process. Now the department says the networks “proudly boycotted” White House events and may have broken the Sherman Act, the 1890 law written to stop giants like Standard Oil. The pool itself is an agreement among competitors to share footage of the president. It ran for decades without anyone calling it an illegal trust, until the networks used it to stand with a rival Trump had shut out. item.title: Here's to ten years of shitposting horses, juking the mods, and turning a gag account into one of the best times I've had on the internet by far!
item.description: (Artist: Ohemo) Technically, this would be my thhhiirrrrteenth year on Imgur if you count my original account that I deleted ages ago once this one started being a lot more fun. If there are any oldheads here who remember when a certain user would post 1,000+ wallpapers in a single dump and hide a pony somewhere in the middle, just to switch the post's thumbnail out for that pony once it hit the front page, that was lil' ol' me. But yeah, a lot's happened since the old days! Back then, horses of the cartoon variety would automatically be downvoted into extinction. I ended up discovering the old @Tagaroo tag list that alerted fellow degens to my posts despite them dropping to the negatives, and eventually a combination of being buoyed back out of oblivion and posting unhinged, ponified memes instead of generic "lol heres my oc no reposts" fanart, I started getting grudging upvotes from non-furries who could admit the gags were worth a chuckle. After a while, the rabid hatred for ponez started to subside and I saw my posts begin to float into the positives without the tag list's help. I started dabbling in making janky GIFs, which evolved into making waaaay too complicated GIFs (the last major one is still my best post to date! https://imgur.com/gallery/tKUbyTe). Hard to believe I made that thing seven years ago, holy shit. But... yeah! Ten flippin' years of doing this is either an accomplishment or a sign of mental deficiency. Why not both? I started teaching myself how to restore antiques thanks to the encouragement I got from Imgurians. I wrote a book and I'm working on its sequel thanks to the support from you folks! So, you know, thank you all for that! I'll keep doing my thing here, no doubt, but I'm also trying to be more active over on my Bluesky account just in case Imgur ever does 404 for good. Things are a little more saucy over on Bsky, but content filters are so much better over there too. If anyone here hasn't tracked me down there yet, it's pretty easy: https://bsky.app/profile/elbowdeepinahorse.bsky.social Anyhow, thank you again to everyone who propped me up, supported me, or lent a kind word of encouragement over the last decade! Here's hoping there are more good times to be had! <3

item.title: Brandon Thomas, developer of ArtCraft, a suite of open-source creative tools meant to replicate Adobe applications for free, has now announced apps to replace Microsoft Office tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, respectively, named GridCraft ...
item.description: Brandon Thomas, developer of ArtCraft, a suite of open-source creative tools meant to replicate Adobe applications for free, has now announced apps to replace Microsoft Office tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, respectively, named GridCraft, DeckCraft, and WordCraft, that are created with Claude. Thomas has shared his new clones to ArtCraft GitHub, making them free for all to download. After our previous story covering ArtCraft, we have since discovered that u/ai_art_is_art is Brandon Thomas, a highly talented software engineer with 15 years of experience under his belt. After his ArtCraft project became popular, many criticisms followed about vibecoded software and AI slop, to which Brandon responded on his X account, saying that he does know how to code. One of the biggest pain points for these software programs is OS compatibility, while Adobe runs on MacOS and Windows, Linux requires additional compatibility layers and Windows emulation to work. One of ArtCraft’s biggest selling points is being able to run all the software across all three platforms while still giving an identical user experience regardless of OS — this is also part of the parity that ArtCraft wants to achieve. While Google provides these tools for free with Google Sheets, Docs, and Slides available on all platforms through a browser, the online-only model takes away the ownership aspect of the software, fearing that one day the tools would suddenly require a subscription and users would not have any say in it. https://www.tomshardware.com/software/microsoft-office/creator-of-free-adobe-clones-unveils-open-source-microsoft-office-excel-powerpoint-and-word-replications-autodesk-tools-and-other-subscription-based-services-may-come-next https://www.tomshardware.com/software/video-editing-graphic-design/solo-developer-rebuilds-adobe-creative-suite-in-rust-using-claude-releases-it-free-to-all-targets-100-percent-parity-in-one-month-despite-piracy-claims-and-safety-warnings
